claim: Stable kinetochore-microtubule attachment is essential for cell division.
source: Stable kinetochore-microtubule attachment is essential for cell division.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about cell division.

claim: Stable kinetochore-microtubule attachment requires recruitment of outer kinetochore microtubule binders by centromere proteins C and T (CENP-C and CENP-T).
source: It requires recruitment of outer kinetochore microtubule binders by centromere proteins C and T (CENP-C and CENP-T).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature establishing this requirement.

claim: CENP-C recruits a single MIS12:NDC80 complex.
source: Whereas CENP-C recruits a single MIS12:NDC80 complex, we show here that CENP-T binds one MIS12:NDC80 and two NDC80 complexes upon phosphorylation by the mitotic CDK1:Cyclin B complex at three distinct CENP-T sites.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on reconstitution experiments.

claim: CENP-T binds one MIS12:NDC80 and two NDC80 complexes upon phosphorylation by the mitotic CDK1:Cyclin B complex at three distinct CENP-T sites.
source: Whereas CENP-C recruits a single MIS12:NDC80 complex, we show here that CENP-T binds one MIS12:NDC80 and two NDC80 complexes upon phosphorylation by the mitotic CDK1:Cyclin B complex at three distinct CENP-T sites.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on reconstitution and mutagenesis experiments.

claim: Visualization of reconstituted complexes by electron microscopy supports the model that CENP-T binds one MIS12:NDC80 and two NDC80 complexes.
source: Visualization of reconstituted complexes by electron microscopy supports this model.
evidence: This statement refers to electron microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Binding of CENP-C and CENP-T to MIS12 is competitive.
source: Binding of CENP-C and CENP-T to MIS12 is competitive, and therefore CENP-C and CENP-T act in parallel to recruit two MIS12 and up to four NDC80 complexes.
evidence: This is a finding based on biochemical binding experiments showing competitive binding.

claim: CENP-C and CENP-T act in parallel to recruit two MIS12 and up to four NDC80 complexes.
source: Binding of CENP-C and CENP-T to MIS12 is competitive, and therefore CENP-C and CENP-T act in parallel to recruit two MIS12 and up to four NDC80 complexes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the competitive binding data and stoichiometry measurements.

claim: Accurate chromosome segregation in eukaryotes requires the coordinated action of hundreds of proteins.
source: Accurate chromosome segregation in eukaryotes requires the coordinated action of hundreds of proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of cell biology.

claim: Centromeric chromatin is epigenetically specified by the enrichment of centromeric protein A (CENP-A), a variant of Histone H3.
source: Subsets of these assemble on centromeric chromatin that is epigenetically specified by the enrichment of centromeric protein A (CENP-A), a variant of Histone H3 (Guse et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Kinetochores form the major point of attachment between centromeres and the mitotic or meiotic spindle.
source: These assemblies, named kinetochores, form the major point of attachment between centromeres and the mitotic or meiotic spindle and couple the force of depolymerizing microtubules to chromosome movement (Cheeseman, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Kinetochores couple the force of depolymerizing microtubules to chromosome movement.
source: These assemblies, named kinetochores, form the major point of attachment between centromeres and the mitotic or meiotic spindle and couple the force of depolymerizing microtubules to chromosome movement (Cheeseman, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Kinetochores function as signaling platforms for the spindle assembly checkpoint.
source: Kinetochores also function as signaling platforms for the spindle assembly checkpoint and delay the onset of chromosome segregation in the presence of erroneous chromosome-spindle attachments (Musacchio, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Kinetochores delay the onset of chromosome segregation in the presence of erroneous chromosome-spindle attachments.
source: Kinetochores also function as signaling platforms for the spindle assembly checkpoint and delay the onset of chromosome segregation in the presence of erroneous chromosome-spindle attachments (Musacchio, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The structural core of the kinetochore assembles from two large multi-subunit complexes, the CCAN and the KMN.
source: The structural core of the kinetochore assembles from two large multi-subunit complexes, the CCAN (constitutive centromere associated network), and the KMN (KNL1 complex, MIS12 complex, NDC80 complex, abbreviated as KNL1C, MIS12C, and NDC80C), which are respectively proximal and distal to the centromeric chromatin (Pesenti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: CCAN and KMN are respectively proximal and distal to the centromeric chromatin.
source: The structural core of the kinetochore assembles from two large multi-subunit complexes, the CCAN (constitutive centromere associated network), and the KMN (KNL1 complex, MIS12 complex, NDC80 complex, abbreviated as KNL1C, MIS12C, and NDC80C), which are respectively proximal and distal to the centromeric chromatin (Pesenti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The affinity of the kinetochore for microtubules in the KMN is predominantly mediated by the NDC80 complex.
source: The affinity of the kinetochore for microtubules in the KMN is predominantly mediated by the NDC80 complex, a heterotetramer with an approximately 50 nm long coiled coil region that separates the microtubule-binding calponin homology (CH) domains of the NDC80 and NUF2 subunits from the SPC24 and SPC25 subunits (Ciferri et al., 2005; Wei et al., 2005, 2007; Ciferri et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: NDC80 complex is a heterotetramer with an approximately 50 nm long coiled coil region.
source: The affinity of the kinetochore for microtubules in the KMN is predominantly mediated by the NDC80 complex, a heterotetramer with an approximately 50 nm long coiled coil region that separates the microtubule-binding calponin homology (CH) domains of the NDC80 and NUF2 subunits from the SPC24 and SPC25 subunits (Ciferri et al., 2005; Wei et al., 2005, 2007; Ciferri et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The coiled coil region of NDC80 complex separates the microtubule-binding calponin homology (CH) domains of the NDC80 and NUF2 subunits from the SPC24 and SPC25 subunits.
source: The affinity of the kinetochore for microtubules in the KMN is predominantly mediated by the NDC80 complex, a heterotetramer with an approximately 50 nm long coiled coil region that separates the microtubule-binding calponin homology (CH) domains of the NDC80 and NUF2 subunits from the SPC24 and SPC25 subunits (Ciferri et al., 2005; Wei et al., 2005, 2007; Ciferri et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: NDC80C is essential to form stable regulated kinetochore-microtubule interactions.
source: NDC80C is essential to form stable regulated kinetochore-microtubule interactions and its localization at the outer kinetochore is thus a prerequisite for faithful chromosome segregation (DeLuca et al., 2005, 2006; Cheeseman et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Localization of NDC80C at the outer kinetochore is a prerequisite for faithful chromosome segregation.
source: NDC80C is essential to form stable regulated kinetochore-microtubule interactions and its localization at the outer kinetochore is thus a prerequisite for faithful chromosome segregation (DeLuca et al., 2005, 2006; Cheeseman et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The recruitment of NDC80C requires the CCAN subunits CENP-C and CENP-T.
source: The recruitment of NDC80C requires the CCAN subunits CENP-C and CENP-T (Liu et al., 2006; Okada et al., 2006; Kwon et al., 2007; Carroll et al., 2010; Gascoigne et al., 2011; Hori et al., 2013) as well as a nuclear envelope breakdown and the activity of mitotic kinases (Gascoigne and Cheeseman, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The recruitment of NDC80C requires nuclear envelope breakdown and the activity of mitotic kinases.
source: The recruitment of NDC80C requires the CCAN subunits CENP-C and CENP-T (Liu et al., 2006; Okada et al., 2006; Kwon et al., 2007; Carroll et al., 2010; Gascoigne et al., 2011; Hori et al., 2013) as well as a nuclear envelope breakdown and the activity of mitotic kinases (Gascoigne and Cheeseman, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: CENP-C directly binds to CENP-A containing nucleosomes.
source: Whereas CENP-C directly binds to CENP-A containing nucleosomes (Carroll et al., 2010) and has been proposed to act as a blueprint for further kinetochore assembly (Klare et al., 2015), CENP-T is integrated in a CENP-TWSX complex that requires its DNA-binding activity (Hori et al., 2008; Nishino et al., 2012), as well as interactions with the CCAN (Carroll et al., 2010; Basilico et al., 2014; Logsdon et al., 2015; Samejima et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015a; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016), to localize to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: CENP-C has been proposed to act as a blueprint for further kinetochore assembly.
source: Whereas CENP-C directly binds to CENP-A containing nucleosomes (Carroll et al., 2010) and has been proposed to act as a blueprint for further kinetochore assembly (Klare et al., 2015), CENP-T is integrated in a CENP-TWSX complex that requires its DNA-binding activity (Hori et al., 2008; Nishino et al., 2012), as well as interactions with the CCAN (Carroll et al., 2010; Basilico et al., 2014; Logsdon et al., 2015; Samejima et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015a; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016), to localize to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior work supported by a citation.

claim: CENP-T is integrated in a CENP-TWSX complex that requires its DNA-binding activity to localize to the kinetochore.
source: Whereas CENP-C directly binds to CENP-A containing nucleosomes (Carroll et al., 2010) and has been proposed to act as a blueprint for further kinetochore assembly (Klare et al., 2015), CENP-T is integrated in a CENP-TWSX complex that requires its DNA-binding activity (Hori et al., 2008; Nishino et al., 2012), as well as interactions with the CCAN (Carroll et al., 2010; Basilico et al., 2014; Logsdon et al., 2015; Samejima et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015a; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016), to localize to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: CENP-TWSX complex requires interactions with the CCAN to localize to the kinetochore.
source: Whereas CENP-C directly binds to CENP-A containing nucleosomes (Carroll et al., 2010) and has been proposed to act as a blueprint for further kinetochore assembly (Klare et al., 2015), CENP-T is integrated in a CENP-TWSX complex that requires its DNA-binding activity (Hori et al., 2008; Nishino et al., 2012), as well as interactions with the CCAN (Carroll et al., 2010; Basilico et al., 2014; Logsdon et al., 2015; Samejima et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015a; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016), to localize to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Depletions of CENP-C or CENP-T affect proper recruitment of MIS12C and NDC80C to the kinetochore.
source: Depletions of CENP-C or CENP-T, or prevention of Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation of CENP-T all affect proper recruitment of MIS12C and NDC80C to the kinetochore (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Gascoigne and Cheeseman, 2013; Hori et al., 2013; Kim and Yu, 2015; Rago et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Prevention of Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation of CENP-T affects proper recruitment of MIS12C and NDC80C to the kinetochore.
source: Depletions of CENP-C or CENP-T, or prevention of Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation of CENP-T all affect proper recruitment of MIS12C and NDC80C to the kinetochore (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Gascoigne and Cheeseman, 2013; Hori et al., 2013; Kim and Yu, 2015; Rago et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Ectopic chromosome anchoring of CENP-C or CENP-T demonstrates the ability of both pathways to recruit outer kinetochore components.
source: Experiments that targeted either CENP-C or CENP-T to an ectopic chromatin array uncoupled these requirements and demonstrated the ability of both pathways to recruit outer kinetochore components (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Hori et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CENP-C and CENP-T recruit NDC80C in distinct ways.
source: An important conclusion from these previous studies is that CENP-C and CENP-T recruit NDC80C in distinct ways (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a conclusion from prior studies, also illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The CENP-C-dependent axis relies on a direct interaction of CENP-C with the MIS12 complex (MIS12C).
source: The CENP-C-dependent axis, which is now understood in detail, relies on a direct interaction of CENP-C with the MIS12 complex (MIS12C) (Screpanti et al., 2011; Przewloka et al., 2011; Dimitrova et al., 2016; Petrovic et al., 2016), which further recruits NDC80C via a direct interaction (Cheeseman et al., 2006; Petrovic et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: MIS12C recruits NDC80C via a direct interaction.
source: The CENP-C-dependent axis, which is now understood in detail, relies on a direct interaction of CENP-C with the MIS12 complex (MIS12C) (Screpanti et al., 2011; Przewloka et al., 2011; Dimitrova et al., 2016; Petrovic et al., 2016), which further recruits NDC80C via a direct interaction (Cheeseman et al., 2006; Petrovic et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: CENP-T interacts directly with NDC80C.
source: It is firmly established that CENP-T interacts directly with NDC80C, with (humans and chicken) or without (budding yeast) prior phosphorylation by CDK1:Cyclin B of sequence motifs in the CENP-T N-terminal region (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: In humans and chicken, CENP-T interaction with NDC80C requires prior phosphorylation by CDK1:Cyclin B of sequence motifs in the CENP-T N-terminal region.
source: It is firmly established that CENP-T interacts directly with NDC80C, with (humans and chicken) or without (budding yeast) prior phosphorylation by CDK1:Cyclin B of sequence motifs in the CENP-T N-terminal region (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: In budding yeast, CENP-T interaction with NDC80C does not require prior phosphorylation by CDK1:Cyclin B.
source: It is firmly established that CENP-T interacts directly with NDC80C, with (humans and chicken) or without (budding yeast) prior phosphorylation by CDK1:Cyclin B of sequence motifs in the CENP-T N-terminal region (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: CENP-T contributes to kinetochore recruitment of MIS12C.
source: Complicating the picture, however, CENP-T also contributes to kinetochore recruitment of MIS12C (Kim and Yu, 2015; Rago et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: MIS12C and CENP-T bind to NDC80C in a competitive manner.
source: This may appear surprising, because MIS12C and CENP-T bind to NDC80C in a competitive manner (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Nishino et al., 2013), suggesting that they can only recruit NDC80C independently from each other.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The CENP-A nucleosome recruits two copies of the CCAN complex.
source: This recently allowed us to report that the CENP-A nucleosome recruits two copies of the CCAN complex (Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from a recent study by the same group, supported by a citation.

claim: CDK1:Cyclin B phosphorylation of CENP-T at Thr11 and Thr85 results in the recruitment of two NDC80Cs.
source: CDK1:Cyclin B phosphorylation reactions with systematically mutated CENP-T substrates revealed that the phosphorylation of CENP-T at Thr11 and Thr85 results in the recruitment of two NDC80Cs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on phosphorylation and binding experiments.

claim: CENP-T interacts directly with MIS12C.
source: We also report that CENP-T interacts directly with MIS12C.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on reconstitution experiments.

claim: CENP-T interaction with MIS12C requires phosphorylation of CENP-T at Ser201.
source: This requires phosphorylation of CENP-T at Ser201, which is encompassed within a non-canonical CDK1 consensus sequence.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on mutagenesis and binding experiments.

claim: Ser201 of CENP-T is encompassed within a non-canonical CDK1 consensus sequence.
source: This requires phosphorylation of CENP-T at Ser201, which is encompassed within a non-canonical CDK1 consensus sequence.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and comparison to known CDK1 consensus sequences.

claim: CENP-T-bound MIS12C recruits additional NDC80C and KNL1C complexes.
source: This CENP-T-bound MIS12C recruits additional NDC80C and KNL1C complexes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on reconstitution experiments.

claim: Phosphorylation of CENP-T at Thr11 or Thr85 is sufficient to recruit SPC24:SPC25.
source: Phosphorylation of CENP-T at Thr11 or Thr85 is thus sufficient to bind SPC24:SPC25.
evidence: This is a finding based on ITC and SEC experiments with mutant CENP-T constructs.

claim: Peptides containing phosphorylated Thr11 showed a binding affinity of 45 μM to SPC24:SPC25.
source: Peptides containing phosphorylated Thr11 or Thr85 showed a binding affinity of 45 μM and 4 μM, respectively, whereas peptides containing phosphorylated Thr27 or Ser47 did not show an interaction with SPC24:SPC25 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from ITC experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Peptides containing phosphorylated Thr85 showed a binding affinity of 4 μM to SPC24:SPC25.
source: Peptides containing phosphorylated Thr11 or Thr85 showed a binding affinity of 45 μM and 4 μM, respectively, whereas peptides containing phosphorylated Thr27 or Ser47 did not show an interaction with SPC24:SPC25 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from ITC experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Peptides containing phosphorylated Thr27 or Ser47 did not show an interaction with SPC24:SPC25.
source: Peptides containing phosphorylated Thr11 or Thr85 showed a binding affinity of 45 μM and 4 μM, respectively, whereas peptides containing phosphorylated Thr27 or Ser47 did not show an interaction with SPC24:SPC25 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from ITC experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ectopic chromosome anchoring of a CENP-T1-250 fragment results in the recruitment of NDC80C when either Thr11 or Thr85 were mutated to Alanine, but not when both were mutated.
source: These results are consistent with in vivo experiments showing that ectopic chromosome anchoring of a CENP-T1-250 fragment results in the recruitment of NDC80C when either Thr11 or Thr85 were mutated to Alanine, but not when both were mutated (Rago et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from a prior study, supported by a citation.

claim: Phosphorylated CENP-T can bind two SPC24:SPC25 units simultaneously.
source: The finding that phosphorylation of CENP-T at either Thr11 or Thr85 is sufficient to recruit SPC24:SPC25, both in vivo (Rago et al., 2015) and in vitro (Figure 1), raises the question whether phosphorylated CENP-T can bind two SPC24:SPC25 units simultaneously.
evidence: This is a hypothesis tested and supported by SEC and EM data in the study.

claim: The coiled-coil of NDC80C spans 51 nm.
source: The coiled-coil of NDC80C spans 51 nm and the NDC80:NUF2 - SPC24:SPC25 end-to-end length is 62 nm (corrected for an estimated 3 nm shadow contribution at both ends) (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a measurement from electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3B and supplement.

claim: The NDC80:NUF2 - SPC24:SPC25 end-to-end length is 62 nm (corrected for an estimated 3 nm shadow contribution at both ends).
source: The coiled-coil of NDC80C spans 51 nm and the NDC80:NUF2 - SPC24:SPC25 end-to-end length is 62 nm (corrected for an estimated 3 nm shadow contribution at both ends) (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a measurement from electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3B and supplement.

claim: The measured end-to-end length of human NDC80C is slightly longer than the 57 nm of yeast NDC80C previously determined using the same technique.
source: This is slightly longer than the 57 nm of yeast NDC80C previously determined using the same technique (Wei et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a comparison to a prior measurement, supported by a citation.

claim: A clear kink in the coiled coil of NDC80C has been previously attributed to a sequence insertion in NDC80.
source: The low-resolution and the flexible appearance of the NDC80C prevent unambiguous assignment of the SPC24:SPC25 and the NDC80:NUF2 modules of the complexes, although a clear kink in the coiled coil, previously attributed to a sequence insertion in NDC80 (Ciferri et al., 2008) marks NDC80:NUF2 in a number of cases (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from EM data, with interpretation based on a prior structural study.

claim: Thr195 and Ser201 of CENP-T have been previously identified as mitotic CENP-T phosphorylation sites.
source: Both Thr195 and Ser201 have been previously identified as mitotic CENP-T phosphorylation sites (Kettenbach et al., 2011), and we confirmed that these residues are also found phosphorylated in CENP-T pulled down with a specific antibody from mitotic HeLa cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a prior study, confirmed by mass spectrometry data in this study.

claim: Thr195 and Ser201 of CENP-T are found phosphorylated in CENP-T pulled down from mitotic HeLa cells.
source: Both Thr195 and Ser201 have been previously identified as mitotic CENP-T phosphorylation sites (Kettenbach et al., 2011), and we confirmed that these residues are also found phosphorylated in CENP-T pulled down with a specific antibody from mitotic HeLa cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from mass spectrometry experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both Thr195 and Ser201 sites were effectively phosphorylated by CDK1 in vitro.
source: Both sites were effectively phosphorylated by CDK1 in vitro (Table 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from in vitro phosphorylation experiments shown in Table 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The peptide carrying phosphorylated Ser201 bound directly to MIS12C in vitro.
source: The peptide carrying phosphorylated Ser201 bound directly to MIS12C in vitro, whereas the equivalent peptide containing phosphorylated Thr195 did not (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments with synthetic peptides shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The peptide containing phosphorylated Thr195 did not bind to MIS12C in vitro.
source: The peptide carrying phosphorylated Ser201 bound directly to MIS12C in vitro, whereas the equivalent peptide containing phosphorylated Thr195 did not (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments with synthetic peptides shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Mutation of Ser201 to alanine abrogates binding of CENP-T to MIS12C.
source: The importance of CENP-T phosphorylation at position Ser201 was recapitulated for the longer CENP-T2-373 construct, where mutation of this residue was shown to abrogate binding to MIS12C (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments with mutant CENP-T shown in Figure 4C and supplement.

claim: Alanine mutation of Thr11 and Thr85 did not affect the binding between CENP-T and MIS12C.
source: Alanine mutation of the phospho-targets Thr11 and Thr85 (Figure 4C) or Thr195 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) did not affect the binding between CENP-T and MIS12C.
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments with mutant CENP-T shown in Figure 4C and supplement.

claim: Alanine mutation of Thr195 did not affect the binding between CENP-T and MIS12C.
source: Alanine mutation of the phospho-targets Thr11 and Thr85 (Figure 4C) or Thr195 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) did not affect the binding between CENP-T and MIS12C.
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments with mutant CENP-T shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Phosphorylation of CENP-T at position Ser201 is both required and sufficient to mediate the MIS12C:CENP-T interaction in vitro.
source: Phosphorylation of CENP-T at position Ser201 is thus both required and sufficient to mediate the MIS12C:CENP-T interaction in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the peptide and mutant binding experiments.

claim: The CENP-T:MIS12C complex sedimented with a frictional ratio of 2.4S and a determined mass of 159 kDa.
source: The CENP-T:MIS12C complex sedimented with a frictional ratio of 2.4S and a determined mass (159 kDa), in close agreement with the theoretical mass of a 1:1 complex (162 kDa, unphosphorylated forms) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a measurement from sedimentation velocity AUC experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The determined mass of the CENP-T:MIS12C complex (159 kDa) is in close agreement with the theoretical mass of a 1:1 complex (162 kDa, unphosphorylated forms).
source: The CENP-T:MIS12C complex sedimented with a frictional ratio of 2.4S and a determined mass (159 kDa), in close agreement with the theoretical mass of a 1:1 complex (162 kDa, unphosphorylated forms) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an interpretation of AUC data comparing measured to theoretical mass.

claim: NDC80C and MIS12C were recruited to CENP-T loci in prometaphase and not in interphase.
source: As previously reported (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Rago et al., 2015), NDC80C and MIS12C were recruited to CENP-T loci in prometaphase and not in interphase (Figure 5A), in agreement with the observed CDK1-dependent recruitment of these complexes to CENP-T in vitro (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a finding from cell-based experiments shown in Figure 5A, consistent with prior studies.

claim: The NDC80C binding mutant CENP-TT11A-T85A failed to recruit not only NDC80C, but also MIS12C, to the lacO locus.
source: The NDC80C binding mutant CENP-TT11A-T85A binds MIS12C in vitro (Figure 4C), but in the context of a LacI-EGFP fusion, it failed to recruit not only NDC80C, but also MIS12C, to the lacO locus, as previously reported (Rago et al., 2015) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from cell-based experiments shown in Figure 5B, consistent with a prior study.

claim: CENP-TS201A recruited NDC80C to the lacO array, but no longer interacted with MIS12C.
source: CENP-TS201A, on the other hand, recruited NDC80C to the lacO array, but no longer interacted with MIS12C (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from cell-based experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: An alanine mutant of Thr195 of CENP-T prevented recruitment of both the MIS12C and the NDC80C to the ectopic lacO site.
source: Interestingly, an alanine mutant of Thr195 of CENP-T prevented recruitment of both the MIS12C and the NDC80C to the ectopic lacO site, even if this residue is dispensable for MIS12C or NDC80C binding in vitro (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, and Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from cell-based experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Thr195 contributes to the efficiency of phosphorylation or to the stability of CENP-T in vivo.
source: We therefore speculate that Thr195 contributes to the efficiency of phosphorylation or to the stability of CENP-T in vivo, an effect that is not recapitulated in vitro, where this residue appears to be dispensable for MIS12C binding.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the discrepancy between in vitro and in vivo results.

claim: Phosphorylated CENP-T integrated in large complexes whose elution volume from the SEC column was smaller than that of MIS12:NDC80 complexes.
source: Phosphorylated CENP-T integrated in large complexes whose elution volume from the SEC column was smaller than that of MIS12:NDC80 complexes.
evidence: This is an observation from SEC experiments.

claim: CENP-Twt associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:3 ratio.
source: Collectively, our results demonstrate that 1) CENP-Twt associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:3 ratio; 2) CENP-TT11A or CENP-TT85A associate with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:2 ratio; and 3) CENP-TT11A-T85A associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:1 ratio.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on SEC and stoichiometry analysis of various CENP-T mutants.

claim: CENP-TT11A or CENP-TT85A associate with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:2 ratio.
source: Collectively, our results demonstrate that 1) CENP-Twt associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:3 ratio; 2) CENP-TT11A or CENP-TT85A associate with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:2 ratio; and 3) CENP-TT11A-T85A associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:1 ratio.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on SEC and stoichiometry analysis of various CENP-T mutants.

claim: CENP-TT11A-T85A associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:1 ratio.
source: Collectively, our results demonstrate that 1) CENP-Twt associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:3 ratio; 2) CENP-TT11A or CENP-TT85A associate with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:2 ratio; and 3) CENP-TT11A-T85A associates with MIS12C and NDC80C in 1:1:1 ratio.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on SEC and stoichiometry analysis of various CENP-T mutants.

claim: MIS12C that interacts with CENP-T phosphorylated at Ser201 can also interact with NDC80C.
source: Thus, MIS12C that interacts with CENP-T phosphorylated at Ser201 can also interact with NDC80C.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on reconstitution experiments showing ternary complex formation.

claim: The CENP-T:MIS12C complex was able to incorporate KNL1C.
source: This complex was also able to incorporate KNL1C, indicating that it can bind an entire KMN assembly, as is the case for MIS12C bound to CENP-C (Petrovic et al., 2016) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from reconstitution experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: MIS12C forms a rod-like 18 nm extension at the SPC24:SPC25 side of NDC80C.
source: As previously described for complexes that were analyzed by electron microscopy after negative staining (Petrovic et al., 2010; Screpanti et al., 2011; Petrovic et al., 2014), analysis of metal-shadowed MIS12C:NDC80C showed that MIS12C forms a rod-like 18 nm extension at the SPC24:SPC25 side of NDC80C (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation from EM data shown in Figure 6B and supplement, consistent with prior studies.

claim: Direct visualization of CENP-T:MIS12C:NDC80C assemblies showed that CENP-T can coordinate MIS12C and a total of three NDC80Cs into a single complex.
source: In agreement with our biochemical analysis, direct visualization of CENP-T:MIS12C:NDC80C assemblies highlighted that CENP-T can coordinate MIS12C and a total of three NDC80Cs into a single complex (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from EM visualization shown in Figure 6B and supplement.

claim: MIS12C3xA was unable to interact with CDK phosphorylated CENP-T.
source: MIS12C3xA was also unable to interact with CDK phosphorylated CENP-T (Figure 7A), suggesting that CENP-T and CENP-C bind to similar sites of MIS12C.
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments shown in Figure 7A.

claim: CENP-T and CENP-C bind to similar sites of MIS12C.
source: MIS12C3xA was also unable to interact with CDK phosphorylated CENP-T (Figure 7A), suggesting that CENP-T and CENP-C bind to similar sites of MIS12C.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the inability of MIS12C3xA to bind either CENP-C or CENP-T.

claim: Both CENP-C1-71 and Ser201 phosphorylated CENP-T195-215 displaced fluorescently labeled CENP-C1-21 from MIS12C.
source: This was confirmed in fluorescence polarization experiments, in which both CENP-C1-71 and Ser201 phosphorylated CENP-T195-215 displaced fluorescently labeled CENP-C1-21 from MIS12C (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence polarization experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The binding affinity between MIS12C and CENP-C1-21 is 128 nM.
source: The relatively high concentration of phosphorylated CENP-T195-215 peptide required to achieve this displacement reflect the tight MIS12C:CENP-C1-21 binding (Kd 128 nM) and the lower MIS12C:CENP-T192-215 binding affinity (Kd ~30 μM) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from fluorescence polarization experiments.

claim: The binding affinity between MIS12C and CENP-T192-215 is approximately 30 μM.
source: The relatively high concentration of phosphorylated CENP-T195-215 peptide required to achieve this displacement reflect the tight MIS12C:CENP-C1-21 binding (Kd 128 nM) and the lower MIS12C:CENP-T192-215 binding affinity (Kd ~30 μM) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from fluorescence polarization experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Longer CENP-C2-545 and CENP-T2-373 fragments bound MIS12C in a competitive manner.
source: Longer CENP-C2-545 and CENP-T2-373 fragments also bound MIS12C in a competitive manner (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments shown in Figure 7C.

claim: CENP-CK10A-Y13A did not disrupt the preformed CENP-T:MIS12C complex.
source: As expected, this strictly depended on the ability of CENP-C to bind MIS12C since the CENP-CK10A-Y13A MIS12C binding mutant (Screpanti et al., 2011) did not disrupt the preformed CENP-T:MIS12C complex (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from SEC experiments shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The binding sites of CENP-C and CENP-T on MIS12C are at least partly overlapping.
source: These results indicate that the binding sites of CENP-C and CENP-T on MIS12C are at least partly overlapping, thus predicting that two distinct MIS12Cs are recruited to CENP-C and CENP-T.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the competitive binding experiments.

claim: Two distinct MIS12Cs are recruited to CENP-C and CENP-T.
source: These results indicate that the binding sites of CENP-C and CENP-T on MIS12C are at least partly overlapping, thus predicting that two distinct MIS12Cs are recruited to CENP-C and CENP-T.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the competitive binding data.

claim: Depletion of CENP-T almost completely abolishes the ultrastructure of the outer kinetochore.
source: Depletion of CENP-T almost completely abolishes the ultrastructure of the outer kinetochore (Hori et al., 2008) and phenocopies the effects of NDC80C depletion (DeLuca et al., 2005), underscoring the importance of CENP-T mediated recruitment of NDC80C to mitotic kinetochores.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Depletion of CENP-T phenocopies the effects of NDC80C depletion.
source: Depletion of CENP-T almost completely abolishes the ultrastructure of the outer kinetochore (Hori et al., 2008) and phenocopies the effects of NDC80C depletion (DeLuca et al., 2005), underscoring the importance of CENP-T mediated recruitment of NDC80C to mitotic kinetochores.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CENP-T depletion lowers NDC80C levels at mitotic kinetochores more than CENP-C depletion.
source: This role is further illustrated by the observation that CENP-T depletion lowers NDC80C levels at mitotic kinetochores more than CENP-C depletion (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Suzuki et al., 2015a), and by experiments showing that replacement of the outer kinetochore binding domain of CENP-C with that of CENP-T supports chromosome segregation in cells depleted of CENP-C (Suzuki et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Replacement of the outer kinetochore binding domain of CENP-C with that of CENP-T supports chromosome segregation in cells depleted of CENP-C.
source: This role is further illustrated by the observation that CENP-T depletion lowers NDC80C levels at mitotic kinetochores more than CENP-C depletion (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Suzuki et al., 2015a), and by experiments showing that replacement of the outer kinetochore binding domain of CENP-C with that of CENP-T supports chromosome segregation in cells depleted of CENP-C (Suzuki et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: One copy of CENP-T recruits two NDC80Cs via phosphorylated CENP-TT11 and CENP-TT85 and an entire KNL1C:MIS12C:NDC80C via phosphorylated CENP-TS201.
source: The analysis of our synthetic outer kinetochores by SEC, SV-AUC, and EM revealed that one copy of CENP-T recruits two NDC80Cs via phosphorylated CENP-TT11 and CENP-TT85 and an entire KNL1C:MIS12C:NDC80C via phosphorylated CENP-TS201.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on multiple experimental approaches.

claim: CENP-C and CENP-T act in parallel to recruit two MIS12Cs, two KNL1Cs, and up to four NDC80Cs in a CDK-regulated manner.
source: Because the binding of CENP-C and CENP-T to MIS12C is competitive, these findings support a model in which CENP-C and CENP-T act in parallel to recruit two MIS12Cs, two KNL1Cs, and up to four NDC80Cs in a CDK-regulated manner (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the findings of the study, illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: Mitotic phosphorylation events trigger the recruitment of four MIS12Cs (and KNL1C) and up to eight NDC80Cs per CENP-A mononucleosome.
source: Because the pseudo-symmetry of the CENP-A nucleosomes allows its binding to two CCAN modules (Weir et al., 2016), we propose that mitotic phosphorylation events trigger the recruitment of four MIS12Cs (and KNL1C) and up to eight NDC80Cs per CENP-A mononucleosome (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a proposal based on extrapolation from the reconstitution data and prior findings about CENP-A nucleosome stoichiometry.

claim: On average, 215 copies of CENP-C and 72 copies of CENP-T recruit a total of 244 NDC80Cs and 151 MIS12Cs to a kinetochore.
source: This analysis revealed that, on average, 215 copies of CENP-C and 72 copies of CENP-T recruit a total of 244 NDC80Cs and 151 MIS12Cs to a kinetochore.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from a prior study cited in the discussion.

claim: Only 82 (of the 215) CENP-C proteins engage in binding MIS12C.
source: However, only 82 (of the 215) CENP-C proteins engage in binding MIS12C, whereas the remaining CENP-C does not contribute to outer kinetochore recruitment.
evidence: This is a finding from a prior study cited in the discussion.

claim: CENP-T is responsible for the recruitment of the remaining MIS12Cs and NDC80Cs not recruited by CENP-C.
source: CENP-T is responsible for the recruitment of the remaining MIS12Cs and NDC80Cs (Suzuki et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is a finding from a prior study cited in the discussion.

claim: The N-terminal tail of CENP-T was seen as a 25 ± 13 nm long flexible extension of the CENP-TW histone-fold domain by high speed atomic force microscopy.
source: Moreover, the N-terminal tail of CENP-T was seen as a 25 ± 13 nm long flexible extension of the CENP-TW histone-fold domain by high speed atomic force microscopy (Suzuki et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from a prior study cited in the discussion.

claim: The N- and C-termini of tagged CENP-T were approximately 30 nm apart in the presence of tension (MG132 treated cells) but only approximately 4 nm apart in the absence of tension (nocodazole treated cells).
source: The flexibility of CENP-T as well as the stretching of CENP-T upon kinetochore-microtubule contacts has been shown before: the N- and C-termini of tagged CENP-T were ~30 nm apart in the presence of tension (MG132 treated cells) but only ~4 nm apart in the absence of tension (nocodazole treated cells), as determined by immunofluorescence and immuno-electron microscopy (Suzuki et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from a prior study cited in the discussion.
